q: We design the first benchmark that evaluates AI coding agents on engineering process discipline through seven measurement pillars, each targeting a distinct dimension of sound software practice
r: Include: new benchmark and trajectory-based metrics for process discipline of coding-agent harnesses (skills, multi-file features), a contribution to the evaluation method.

q: We showed that this proxy can detach from the deliverable in two opposite ways
r: Include: controlled experiment with repetitions building a component library from a reference spec, studying how oracle exposure changes what agents deliver (evaluation method).

q: We introduce SWE-Together, a 109-task benchmark reconstructed from real multi-turn user interactive coding-agent sessions, together with a pipeline that converts recorded sessions into verifiable tasks.
r: Include: new interactive benchmark with user simulator and correction metrics, replicates, on real feature-level coding sessions, so the contribution is the evaluation method.

q: We adopt 25 tasks from each of three frontier SWE benchmarks (75 total): SWE-bench Pro, SWE Atlas (Refactoring), and DeepSWE
r: EC6: tasks are reused SWE-bench Pro, refactoring and issue-style tasks, so it is issue repair style, excluded even though a user simulator is added.

q: We study this problem through a first-person case study: a 12-week development effort in which a single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system.
r: Include: project-level application built with coding agents over 12 weeks, studying governance controls (cost, human judgment) for agentic development.

q: we do not introduce another benchmark or report a new agent leaderboard. We audit the released artifacts behind existing repository-level benchmarks
r: EC6: audit of performance-optimization benchmarks (GSO, SWE-Perf, SWE-fficiency), patch-level optimization is not application development from requirements and is a specialised domain.

q: We release an initial fold of 16 coding agent scenarios.
r: Include: new benchmark whose contribution is the evaluation method (trajectory reviews, quality index, variance and bias checks) on developer coding workflows.

q: DeepSWE is a benchmark of 113 original, long-horizon software engineering tasks for evaluating coding agents.
r: Include: new benchmark of original feature-level repository tasks with sampling, uncertainty quantification and cost metrics, not issue repair.

q: can an agentic LLM generate an end-to-end software artifact that is both deployable and behaviorally correct under execution?
r: Include: new benchmark for building whole backend services from a specification, with an oracle co-evolution method, i.e. project-level development and evaluation method.

q: Both evaluation periods utilized a Specification-Driven Development (SDD) methodology to guide the autonomous agents.
r: Include: cost and code-quality comparison of cloud vs on-premise models in agentic development with defect metrics and statistics, using an SDD workflow.
